description: Intelligent Lunar Landing Site Selection & Optimization System
summary:
SELENE-X is an interactive lunar mission planning platform designed to help users explore and evaluate potential landing sites near the Moon’s South Pole. It addresses the challenges of lunar exploration by combining real NASA scientific data with interactive 3D visualization and engineering simulations.

Users can explore three potential landing sites—Shackleton Rim, Malapert Massif, and Connecting Ridge—or select custom coordinates on the 3D Moon. The platform uses NASA/JPL Horizons DE441 data to analyze sunlight conditions and potential Earth visibility windows, alongside NASA’s LRO LOLA elevation data to examine lunar terrain. It also includes a customizable solar energy simulator, intelligent landing-site alerts, mission scenario comparisons, and an integrated AI assistant.

By transforming complex lunar datasets into accessible, interactive insights, SELENE-X helps users understand how environmental conditions and engineering choices can affect mission planning. Its goal is to support more informed decisions and contribute to the planning of future lunar exploration missions.
details:
SELENE-X – Interactive Lunar Mission Planning Platform

SELENE-X is an interactive lunar mission planning platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It helps users explore, analyze, and compare potential landing sites near the Moon's South Pole by combining scientific lunar datasets, interactive 3D visualization, and engineering simulations.

The platform provides an interactive 3D Moon where users can explore three predefined landing sites: Shackleton Rim, Malapert Massif, and Connecting Ridge. Users can also enter custom coordinates to investigate additional lunar locations, making the exploration experience more flexible and user-driven.

SELENE-X integrates NASA/JPL Horizons DE441 astronomical data, containing hourly samples of the apparent positions of the Sun and Earth from 2026 to 2031 for the selected landing sites. This information supports the analysis of sunlight availability, shadow periods, and potential Earth visibility windows. Additionally, the platform uses NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) LOLA dataset, LDEM_85S_40M_FLOAT, with approximately 40-meter spatial resolution, to visualize elevation variations and examine lunar terrain profiles.

A major feature is the customizable Solar Energy Simulator, which allows users to modify solar panel area, efficiency, inclination, orientation, battery capacity, and mission power consumption. The simulator estimates electricity generation and battery performance under different configurations, helping users understand how engineering decisions may affect mission energy resources.

Other features include interactive scientific graphs and charts, Intelligent Landing Site Alerts that highlight potentially unfavorable conditions, Mission Scenario Comparison for evaluating different locations and configurations, and the integrated SELENE-X AI Assistant for exploring lunar science and mission-related questions. The NASA Media Gallery also connects users to NASA's official image and video archive through the NASA Images API.

The platform was developed using React, TypeScript, and Vite, and is designed for deployment through GitHub Pages. Its core Horizons and LOLA datasets are stored locally to support offline access. SHA-256 verification is used to check dataset integrity and detect accidental modifications or corruption. The NASA Media Gallery requires an internet connection.

SELENE-X's main innovation is bringing 3D lunar exploration, custom location selection, real NASA astronomical and topographic data, energy simulations, automated alerts, and scenario comparison together in one interactive environment. Instead of simply presenting scientific information, it allows users to investigate how lunar environmental conditions and engineering configurations can influence mission planning.

During development, important considerations included scientific data reliability, spatial resolution, coordinate accuracy, time-dependent astronomical conditions, energy requirements, potential communication limitations, offline data availability, and user accessibility. The platform presents analytical estimates and decision-support information rather than claiming to provide certified landing safety assessments or guaranteed mission outcomes.

Ultimately, SELENE-X aims to make complex lunar data easier to explore and understand, encourage scientific investigation, and support more informed engineering decisions for future lunar exploration missions.
